narrative:
The model determined that you have a 41% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough to cross the bank's threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your installment rate as a percentage of disposable income, and the total amount of credit you requested. 

Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single most important reason for the denial. Among approved applicants, only about 13% have a negative balance, while the majority (59%) have no checking account at all. This negative status pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk.

Your requested installment rate of 1% of disposable income worked in your favor. Most approved applicants have a higher rate (average around 3%), so this lower commitment helped pull the prediction back toward approval.

The loan amount of 2,039 DM you asked for was also lower than the average of roughly 3,020 DM among those who were approved. This smaller request likewise helped reduce the risk score.

Even though two of the top factors worked in your favor, the negative checking account status carried more weight than the positive effects from the other two.

You should focus on bringing your checking account balance back into positive territory and maintaining it for several months. Once that improves, reapply. This single change is likely to have the biggest impact on future decisions. (218 words)
